answer: Picture the trust graph as an orchard where honest agents are densely cross-pollinated: many bonded edges, high conductance. A sybil ring is a walled ivory haven, joined to the real grove by only a thin cut of edges. Each epoch a rotating jury samples the graph conductance and spectral gap; any cluster dangling off a sparse bottleneck has its stake slashed. To fake that density an attacker must buy N genuine bonded edges to distinct honest peers, each posting real collateral, so N identities cost N times the staked capital and cheap rings stay easy to catch.
